chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

q1_what_did_you_play: Thoma — Crimson Ooyoroi into Nibbit first, then All Streams Flow to the Sea into Nibbit. That is all 3 energy (2 + 1) and it is the most damage the hand can produce: 8 + 9 = 17, taking Nibbit from 24 to 7, while Thoma's 3 Block still comes along for free. Nibbit's 12 leaves me at 5 HP instead of 2. Nothing in the hand reaches 24, so killing it this turn was never on the table; the goal was to leave it in one-hit range for next turn while surviving the telegraphed 12. I led with Thoma because it is the 2-cost and I wanted it down before I could be short on energy, and because if the Pyro it applies interacts with the Hydro that follows, the order costs me nothing and might gain something — I am not counting on that, the 17 is all printed numbers.
q2_other_line_considered: Water's Edge plus All Streams Flow to the Sea — 15 damage for only 2 energy, banking one. I dropped it because energy does not carry and the hand does not survive the turn, so the 'saved' point is worth nothing and it is simply 2 less damage and 3 less Block than what I played. I also weighed Thoma plus Water's Edge (14 damage, same 3 Block), but that is the chosen line with 3 damage shaved off, so it is dominated outright. Honestly, once I noticed Thoma's Block is attached to the biggest attack, the turn stopped being close: my line beats both alternatives on every axis at once.
q3_what_it_gave_up: Water's Edge sits unplayed — 6 damage and a Hydro application left on the table, since 2+1+1 exceeds 3 energy. That is the whole cost; I gave up no Block and no tempo, because the line that keeps Water's Edge would have to cut All Streams and lose more damage than it gains. I also gave up any chance of ending the turn above 5 HP, but no configuration of this hand does better than 3 Block against a 12.
q4_different_intent: Yes. Against a bigger telegraph the Block stops being incidental and starts being the whole point. If Nibbit had shown 15 or 16, Thoma becomes mandatory for its 3 Block and I would still take the same two cards — but if the hand had offered more Block, I would have taken it over damage. More concretely: if the intent were an attack in the 15–17 band, the 3 Block is the margin between living and dying and I would refuse any line that skips Thoma, including the 15-damage double-Hydro line I considered. If the intent were a Defend or a buff — no attack at all — the Block is dead weight, and I would want the cheapest maximum damage instead: Water's Edge plus All Streams for 15 at 2 energy is still 2 short of 17, so I would probably still play the same two cards, but the reasoning changes from 'survive and set up' to pure damage. So the intent does not always move my hands, but it moves what I am buying.
